evidence.quote: We present a longitudinal causal study of agent adoption in open-source repositories using staggered difference-in-differences with matched controls.
We estimate average and dynamic treatment effects using the imputation-based DiD estimator of Borusyak et al. [18]
After filtering, our heterogeneous samples contain 401 AF repositories matched to 606 controls and 117 IF repositories matched to 73 controls.
We build on the AIDev dataset (v3) [28], which links GitHub repositories to AI-generated pull requests
We restrict analysis to repositories with ≥10 stars to exclude toy and spam projects and require ≥10 agentic PRs per treated repository to ensure non-trivial exposure.
We measure development velocity via monthly commit counts and lines added; software quality via static-analysis warnings, duplicatedline density, and cognitive complexity using SonarQube[11].
AF repos see large average gains (+36.3% commits; +76.6% lines added), whereas IF repos show minimal changes (+3.1%; −6.3%).
quality risks are persistent across settings, with static-analysis warnings and cognitive complexity rising by roughly 18% and 39%, indicating sustained agent-induced technical debt
